passages.provision_quote: (c) (1) Following the implementation of the minimum wage increase specified in subparagraph (F) of paragraph (2) of subdivision (b), on or before August 1 of that year, and on or before each August 1 thereafter, the Director of Finance shall calculate an adjusted minimum wage. The calculation shall increase the minimum wage by the lesser of 3.5 percent and the rate of change in the averages of the most recent July 1 to June 30, inclusive, period over the preceding July 1 to June 30, inclusive, period for the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics nonseasonally adjusted United States Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (U.S. CPI-W). The result shall be rounded to the nearest ten cents ($0.10). Each adjusted minimum wage increase calculated under this subdivision shall take effect on the following January 1.
passages.note: The bill text prints the operative wage provisions: a general step raise to fifteen dollars per hour in Labor Code 1182.12(b) and the automatic annual CPI-W adjustment in 1182.12(c), which needs no further legislation.

rows.reasoning: Allen voted Aye on Senate concurrence in SB 3 (2015-2016), a general minimum-wage law that both raises the floor in steps to fifteen dollars per hour for all industries and then directs the Director of Finance to annually "calculate an adjusted minimum wage" by the U.S. CPI-W, taking effect each January 1. That matches both clauses of the rung that would "Raise the wage floor and tie it to the cost of living, so it rises automatically each year without new legislation", and the automatic index excludes the rung that would "adjust it only when lawmakers vote to". The bill's second subject (paid sick days for in-home supportive services providers) is a related Labor Code provision keyed to the same wage schedule, not an omnibus, so the wage sections govern the vote.
